textbookText: 21. If the empirical formula of a compound is CH₂O and its molecular mass is 180 g/mol (empirical mass = 30), the molecular formula is: A) C₆H₁₂O₆ (n = 180/30 = 6) B) C₂H₄O₂ C) CH₂O itself (n=1) D) C₃H₆O₃

22. Which of the following correctly reflects the "law of reciprocal proportions"? A) When two elements combine separately with a fixed mass of a third element, the ratio of their masses is the same (or simple multiple) as when they combine directly with each other B) Elements never combine in fixed ratios C) It applies only to gaseous elements D) It contradicts the law of conservation of mass
23. The volume of gas at STP produced from 0.5 mole of CO₂ is: A) 11.2 L B) 22.4 L C) 5.6 L D) 44.8 L

24. Which statement about "excess reagent" is correct? A) It is the reactant left over/unreacted after the limiting reagent is fully consumed B) It determines the maximum yield of product C) It is always consumed completely along with the limiting reagent D) It has no role in determining product quantity, ever relevant to calculations

25. Molar concentration (molarity) is defined as: A) Moles of solute per litre of solution B) Moles of solute per kg of solvent C) Grams of solute per litre of solution D) Moles of solvent per litre of solution

26. In redox stoichiometry, the number of electrons lost by the reducing agent must equal: A) The number of electrons gained by the oxidizing agent B) The number of moles of the reducing agent C) Zero, since redox reactions conserve mass only D) The atomic number of the reducing agent
27. What mass of CaCO₃ (molar mass 100 g/mol) is needed to produce 1 mole of CO₂ upon complete decomposition (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂)? A) 100 g B) 56 g C) 44 g D) 200 g

28. Which of these is an example of applying stoichiometry in real industry (extraordinary fact)? A) The Haber process uses precise N₂:H₂ mole ratios (1:3) to optimize ammonia yield industrially B) Stoichiometry is used only in academic laboratory exercises, not industry C) Industrial processes ignore mole ratios and rely only on trial and error D) Stoichiometric calculations apply only to organic compounds
29. The number of atoms of oxygen in 1 mole of Na₂CO₃ is: A) 3 × 6.022 × 10²³ B) 6.022 × 10²³ C) 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ D) 6 × 6.022 × 10²³

30. A limiting reagent problem is best solved by: A) Converting all reactants to moles and comparing mole ratio to the balanced equation's stoichiometric ratio B) Comparing the masses of reactants directly without converting to moles C) Assuming the reactant present in larger mass is always limiting D) Ignoring the balanced equation and using volumes only
